paper_metadata.title: Acute thalamic connectivity precedes chronic post-concussive symptoms in mild traumatic brain injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large, multicenter prospective cohort (CENTER-TBI) with well-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria. The sample is representative of the target population (GCS 13-15, normal CT), and baseline characteristics are thoroughly described and compared with controls.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We compared structural MRI and resting state functional MRI in 108 patients with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) of 13-15 and normal CT, and 76 controls.
items.reasoning: The target population is clearly defined by clinical severity (GCS) and imaging status (normal CT).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Data for the analyses in this manuscript were obtained from subjects recruited to the MRI sub-study of CENTER-TBI between December 2014 and December 2017
items.reasoning: Recruitment is part of a large-scale, standardized European multicenter study with established protocols.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between December 2014 and December 2017
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Matched healthy controls (n = 76) were recruited from the same centres as patients and contemporaneously imaged on the same MRI systems.
items.reasoning: Recruitment occurred across multiple European centers participating in CENTER-TBI.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria were that subjects were aged 18–70 years with no medical history of previous concussion or neuropsychiatric disease. We included 108 patients who additionally sustained a mTBI [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 13–15], required a head CT according to local criteria on initial presentation, showed no CT abnormalities
items.reasoning: Criteria are explicit regarding age, prior history, and acute clinical presentation.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (thalamic functional connectivity) is measured using state-of-the-art fMRI preprocessing (fmriprep) and standardized atlases. The use of NeuroCombat for site harmonization and rigorous motion scrubbing limits measurement bias.

items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Three lines of thalamic functional connectivity were investigated... average thalamocortical connectivity... functional connectivity between thalamic ROIs... local brain-wide functional connectivity changes
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly defined as specific fMRI-derived connectivity metrics.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).

items.reasoning: Standardized, validated pipelines and denoising techniques were used.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

items.reasoning: Standardized protocols were used across sites, and statistical harmonization was applied to address site-specific variance.
